gloss: formal kimono with family crest; crested garment

definitions.explanation: A formal Japanese garment featuring the wearer's family crest (mon). The most formal type of traditional Japanese attire.

examples.japanese: {結婚式|けっこんしき}で{紋付|もんつき}{袴|はかま}を{着|き}た。
examples.english: I wore a crested kimono with hakama at the wedding.
examples.notes: {紋付|もんつき}{袴|はかま} is the full formal outfit for men

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{紋付|もんつき}を{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ。
examples.english: I inherited my grandfather's crested kimono.

examples.japanese: {五|いつ}つ{紋|もん}の{紋付|もんつき}が{最|もっと}も{格式|かくしき}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: A crested kimono with five family crests is the most formal.
examples.notes: {五|いつ}つ{紋|もん} = five crests (the most formal level)

notes:
TRADITIONAL JAPANESE FORMAL WEAR:
{紋付|もんつき} refers to any garment bearing a family crest ({家紋|かもん}). Most commonly refers to a formal black kimono worn by men at ceremonies.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
The number of crests indicates the level of formality:
- {五|いつ}つ{紋|もん} (5 crests): Most formal, for weddings, funerals
- {三|みっ}つ{紋|もん} (3 crests): Semi-formal
- {一|ひと}つ{紋|もん} (1 crest): Less formal

FULL FORMAL OUTFIT:
For men: {紋付|もんつき}{羽織|はおり}{袴|はかま} (crested haori jacket with hakama pants)
For women: {黒留|くろとめ}{袖|そで} with family crests

OCCASIONS:
- {結婚式|けっこんしき}: Weddings
- {葬式|そうしき}: Funerals
- {成人式|せいじんしき}: Coming-of-age ceremony
- {茶道|さどう}: Tea ceremony (formal occasions)

NOTE: Rental services ({貸衣装|かしいしょう}) are common since many families no longer own {紋付|もんつき}.
